purpose: Proposed exercise catalog and decision metadata; not a deployed app configuration or clinical rehabilitation protocol.

field_semantics.equipment_options_all_of: Outer array is OR; each inner list is AND. Environmental supports count as requirements.
field_semantics.primary_display_group: Navigation label only; not an exclusive target or proof of equal training effect.
field_semantics.prime_movers: Qualitative anatomical targets, not measured fractional volume credits.
field_semantics.default_pool: Eligible for consideration after user-specific equipment, skill, tolerance and time filters; never schedule every eligible record.
field_semantics.priority: P1 = next release; P2 = optional expansion; keep = retained default candidate; optional/advanced = retained opt-in; retire = legacy record excluded from new automatic plans.
field_semantics.evidence_basis: Direct evidence applies only within the cited study conditions. Pattern extrapolation is explicitly not a direct trial of the exact entry.
field_semantics.laterality: Unilateral repetitions are per side. Alternating repetitions are also entered per side in this proposed schema.
field_semantics.progression: No universal numerical ranking across exercises; load, assistance, ROM and support configuration remain distinct.

strength_exercises.name: Barbell deadlift
strength_exercises.selection_note: Include for conventional-deadlift goals; not a required hypertrophy or beginner exercise.
strength_exercises.evidence_scope_note: References support only the stated pattern or tested variation; no universal superiority or injury-safety claim.

cardio_modalities.name: Walking
cardio_modalities.note: Includes flat and incline walking; incline is a setting, not a separate required mode.

cardio_modalities.name: Jogging or running
cardio_modalities.note: Walk-run intervals provide an entry route; do not equate slow speed with low individual effort.

cardio_modalities.name: Elliptical
cardio_modalities.note: Useful alternative when running is not preferred.

cardio_modalities.name: Rowing ergometer
cardio_modalities.note: Needs technique familiarization and contributes lower-back, grip and posterior-chain fatigue.

cardio_modalities.name: Stair climber or stair walking
cardio_modalities.note: Budget leg fatigue; stairs require balance and environment checks.

cardio_modalities.name: Jump rope
cardio_modalities.note: Skill and repeated impact matter; possessing a rope does not make it the default warm-up.

cardio_modalities.name: Indoor marching or low-impact movement
cardio_modalities.note: Accessible weather-independent option; verify that effort reaches the intended intensity.

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.design: Overview of 137 reviews; >30,000 participants; search through October 2024.
sources.finding: Progressive resistance training improves multiple outcomes. Regular training of major muscle groups is the foundation; prescriptions should reflect the goal.
sources.application_and_limit: Broad support for home and gym modes; strongest evidence for programming principles, not a ranking of individual exercises. The 2026 publication does not itself include all 2025-26 research.
sources.access: Indexed abstract plus official ACSM summary

sources.title: The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains
sources.design: 67 studies, 2,058 participants; about 79% male; mean age about 25.
sources.finding: More weekly sets predicted greater gains with diminishing returns. Frequency had a clearer independent relationship with strength than with hypertrophy. Fractional accounting for indirect sets fitted the data best.
sources.application_and_limit: Support adjustable weekly volume and distinguish direct from indirect work. A 0.5 contribution is a modeling convention, not a universal biological conversion.

sources.title: Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
sources.design: Strength network: 178 studies / 5,097 participants; hypertrophy: 119 / 3,364.
sources.finding: Many prescriptions improved outcomes. Heavier loading was especially relevant to maximal strength; multiple sets were useful for hypertrophy.
sources.application_and_limit: Provide strength and muscle-growth settings without making a single rep range the only effective choice. Network rankings do not prove one universal best program.

sources.title: Superset Versus Traditional Resistance Training Prescriptions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Exploring Acute and Chronic Effects on Mechanical, Metabolic, and Perceptual Variables
sources.design: 19 studies, 313 participants; mixed acute and longer-term outcomes.
sources.finding: Supersets shortened sessions and generally preserved adaptations, while raising perceived effort. Same-muscle pairings could reduce completed training volume.
sources.application_and_limit: Offer noncompeting pairs as a time-saving option. The chronic evidence is smaller than the total study count; preserve performance and recovery.

sources.title: No Time to Lift? Designing Time-Efficient Training Programs for Strength and Hypertrophy: A Narrative Review
sources.design: Narrative synthesis focused on limited-time training.
sources.finding: Bilateral multijoint exercises, selective warm-ups, and economical set structures can reduce the time burden.
sources.application_and_limit: A useful design framework, not a trial validating a particular 20-minute app routine. Avoid assuming unilateral work is always the best upgrade.
sources.access: PubMed abstract and indexed full-text sections

sources.title: Without Fail: Muscular Adaptations in Single-Set Resistance Training Performed to Failure or with Repetitions-in-Reserve
sources.design: 42 trained young men and women; one set of nine exercises, twice weekly, for eight weeks.
sources.finding: Both failure and two-repetitions-in-reserve groups improved most outcomes. Some muscle-growth outcomes modestly favored failure; strength changes were similar.
sources.application_and_limit: Justifies a low-volume fallback. It does not establish that one set maximizes gains or that a shorter four-exercise plan reproduces this trial.

sources.title: Exploring the Dose-Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Series of Meta-Regressions
sources.design: Exploratory meta-regressions; repetitions in reserve were estimated from study descriptions.
sources.finding: Training closer to failure was associated with more hypertrophy; strength gains were less sensitive across the studied range.
sources.application_and_limit: Teach effort and use challenging sets, but do not force failure or describe a precise RIR cutoff as settled science.

sources.title: Effect of free-weight vs. machine-based strength training on maximal strength, hypertrophy and jump performance - a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.journal: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
sources.design: 13 studies; only five contributed hypertrophy outcomes.
sources.finding: No clear hypertrophy advantage for either mode; strength improvements were substantially specific to the trained and tested mode.
sources.application_and_limit: Machines belong in the main gym pool. This is not proof that every machine and free-weight variation is equivalent, or that one mode is universally safer.

sources.title: Effects of training with elastic resistance versus conventional resistance on muscular strength: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of elastic versus conventional resistance.
sources.finding: Elastic resistance can improve strength with broadly comparable results to conventional resistance in the included comparisons.
sources.application_and_limit: Bands are a legitimate home option. Evidence here concerns strength, not proof of equal hypertrophy for every band exercise. Standardize anchor position and band setup.

sources.title: Low-load bench press and push-up induce similar muscle hypertrophy and strength gain
sources.design: 18 young men; eight weeks, twice weekly; load-matched push-ups and low-load bench press.
sources.finding: The groups had similar muscle-growth and strength improvements under the tested conditions.
sources.application_and_limit: Keep scalable push-ups as a principal home chest exercise. Small, narrow trial; do not extrapolate to equal maximal-strength outcomes at every ability level.

sources.title: Greater Hamstrings Muscle Hypertrophy but Similar Damage Protection after Training at Long versus Short Muscle Lengths
sources.design: Within-person comparison of seated versus prone knee-flexion training.
sources.finding: Whole-hamstring volume increased more with seated than prone curls (about 14% versus 9%); the difference involved the biarticular muscles.
sources.application_and_limit: Add knee-flexion work and favor seated curls when available and comfortable. This was not a direct comparison of curls versus RDLs or sliders.

sources.title: Hypertrophic Effects of Single- versus Multi-Joint Exercise: A Direct Comparison between Knee Extension and Leg Press
sources.journal: Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise 58(7):1566-1580; online February 2026
sources.design: 17 untrained adults; opposite legs trained for 12 weeks; MRI outcomes.
sources.finding: Rectus femoris growth favored knee extension (13.2% versus 1.1%); other quadriceps regions and total quadriceps were more similar. Leg press also grew gluteus maximus and adductor magnus.
sources.application_and_limit: Include leg press as a compound option and leg extension as complementary quad work. The small single study does not make isolation mandatory in every short workout.
sources.access: Indexed PubMed abstract and publisher record

sources.title: Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position
sources.journal: European Journal of Sport Science 23(7):1240-1250; online 2022
sources.design: 21 adults; opposite arms; cable extensions twice weekly for 12 weeks.
sources.finding: Overhead extensions produced greater triceps growth than neutral-arm extensions in this protocol, particularly in the long head.
sources.application_and_limit: Retain the overhead pattern and add a cable version plus pressdowns as an alternative. The direct trial used cables, not the existing dumbbell variation.

sources.title: Triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training
sources.design: 14 untrained adults; opposite legs; 12 weeks.
sources.finding: Standing raises produced substantially more gastrocnemius growth; soleus growth was similar between conditions.
sources.application_and_limit: Prioritize a straight-knee calf option. Seated raises remain useful alternatives, but the trial does not show that seated work is required for soleus growth.

sources.title: Hip thrust and back squat training elicit similar gluteus muscle hypertrophy and transfer similarly to the deadlift
sources.design: Nine-week randomized training comparison using MRI; final peer-reviewed version.
sources.finding: Gluteal hypertrophy was similar, thigh growth favored squats, and strength gains favored the practiced exercise.
sources.application_and_limit: Squats and hip thrusts are legitimate choices for different priorities. Acute muscle-activation rankings alone should not determine the catalog.

sources.title: Dumbbell versus cable lateral raises for lateral deltoid hypertrophy: an experimental study
sources.design: 24 completers; trained men and women; opposite arms; eight weeks; matched motion range.
sources.finding: Dumbbells and cables produced similar lateral-deltoid growth under these conditions.
sources.application_and_limit: Add cables for preference and availability, not as a superior level unlocked after dumbbells. Different motion ranges were not tested.

sources.title: Lengthened partial repetitions elicit similar muscular adaptations as full range of motion repetitions during resistance training in trained individuals
sources.design: 30 trained participants; opposite arms; eight-week upper-body intervention.
sources.finding: Lengthened partials and full-range training produced similar measured arm hypertrophy and pulldown strength-endurance changes.
sources.application_and_limit: Use controlled, tolerable full range by default; retain lengthened partials as an optional technique. This is not evidence for replacing all full-range training.

sources.title: Give it a rest: a systematic review with Bayesian meta-analysis on the effect of inter-set rest interval duration on muscle hypertrophy
sources.journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living 6:1429789
sources.design: Nine studies; wide and overlapping estimates.
sources.finding: Results suggested a small benefit from resting more than 60 seconds; additional differences above 90 seconds were not clearly detected.
sources.application_and_limit: Do not achieve short sessions by indiscriminately removing rest. Adjust rest to restore useful performance rather than treating one duration as a universal optimum.

sources.title: Efficacy of Split Versus Full-Body Resistance Training on Strength and Muscle Growth: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis
sources.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 38(7):1330-1340
sources.design: 14 studies, 392 participants.
sources.finding: Split and full-body routines produced similar outcomes when training volume was matched.
sources.application_and_limit: Default to full-body sessions for two or three available days; allow splits for preference and scheduling. Full-body is a convenience choice, not a universal physiological winner.

sources.title: Does Varying Resistance Exercises Promote Superior Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains? A Systematic Review
sources.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 36(6):1753-1762
sources.design: Eight studies, 241 participants, all young men.
sources.finding: Planned variation may aid regional development; excessive random variation and redundant choices can impede useful training continuity.
sources.application_and_limit: Keep a small stable exercise menu across a training block. Change exercises for a reason, with a separate performance history for each variation.

sources.title: The Effects of Advanced Resistance Training Prescription Methods on Strength, Power, Hypertrophy, and Performance Adaptations in Healthy Adults: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-analysis
sources.design: Review and network meta-analysis of traditional training and seven advanced methods.
sources.finding: Advanced methods did not consistently outperform traditional training for strength, power, or hypertrophy in untrained to moderately trained adults.
sources.application_and_limit: Treat techniques such as advanced set structures as optional tools; simple progression remains a sound default. Highly trained populations were less well represented.

sources.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
sources.design: International public-health guideline, with official WHO current guidance cross-check.
sources.finding: Adults should accumulate 150-300 minutes of moderate or 75-150 minutes of vigorous aerobic activity weekly, or an equivalent mix, alongside strengthening at least twice weekly.
sources.application_and_limit: Count walking outside formal workouts. Short strength sessions do not automatically fulfill aerobic targets; activity below the target still has value.
sources.access: Indexed guideline abstract and WHO official guidance

sources.title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training on Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Cardiometabolic Health in Real-World Settings: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.design: 31 studies, 1,119 participants; controlled and uncontrolled reports; search through December 2025.
sources.finding: Real-world HIIT was associated with improved cardiorespiratory fitness and selected cardiometabolic outcomes.
sources.application_and_limit: Offer intervals on suitable modes, including bikes. Within-group pooled changes do not establish superiority over continuous training or identify a universally best interval protocol.

sources.title: Effects of resistance training variables on muscle hypertrophy in resistance-trained individuals: A systematic review
sources.journal: Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies 48:1149-1152; online August 21, 2026
sources.design: Six studies in a qualitative synthesis; search through April 2025.
sources.finding: The review emphasizes training volume and effort as central contributors, with less consistent independent effects of other variables.
sources.application_and_limit: Recent corroboration, given limited weight because the synthesis is small. Do not optimize raw tonnage across exercises: load times reps is not a comparable hypertrophy dose across movements.
